podcast.body: Audioslave's 2002 debut album cover, designed by legendary artist Storm Thorgerson, depicts a golden, flame-like sculpture situated in a desolate landscape, accompanied by a solitary figure in a red shirt and shorts. Thorgerson described the music as "brooding and sultry" and explained the flame symbolizes "the eternal flame, or the flame of remembrance," embodying the band's previous incarnations, Soundgarden and Rage Against the Machine. The image is a real, posed photograph taken on the volcanic island of Lanzarote. "The cover was designed by Storm Thorgerson, probably the most famous album art creator of all time."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Stories Behind Iconic Album Covers Part 2

podcast.body: Audioslave's self-titled debut album was released in 2002. A complex label deal was worked out: the first album was released jointly by Epic (Rage Against the Machine's label) and Interscope (Chris Cornell's label). The second album was solely on Interscope, and the third was Interscope for the US and Epic for the rest of the world. "The first album would be released by both Epic, Rage Against the Machine's label, and Interscope, Chris's label."
